title: Microsoft Copilot app: Chat suggests a better-fit mode such as Cowork
summary: Hold: the access-control route skips the Identity policy-type choice required by the spending-policy wizard. The rollout, suggestion behaviour and Cowork billing controls are otherwise supported; the licensing description and reporting citations need small clarifications.

claims.claim: Chat in the Copilot app suggests a better-fit mode after the user sends a prompt, where applicable.
claims.quote: The Chat experience in the Copilot app will suggest a better-fit mode based on the user's prompt, if applicable.

claims.claim: Cowork is the example destination, with other supported modes suggested as they become available.
claims.quote: For example, it will suggest Cowork or other supported modes as they become available.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The suggestion card explains the better-fit mode.
claims.quote: Users will see a suggestion card after they send a prompt in Chat, with an explanation of the better-fit mode and an option for the user to switch to the suggested mode.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The banner lets the user choose whether to switch or remain in Chat.
claims.quote: In the banner, the user will see an option to switch to the suggested experience (ie. Cowork) or remain in Chat.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Chat conversation context is attached to the prompt in the destination mode.
claims.quote: Their chat conversation will be attached to the prompt in the new mode to maintain context.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Choosing to switch opens the suggested experience with the prompt already sent.
claims.quote: If the user selects the option to switch, they will be brought directly to the suggested experience with the prompt already sent, along with the context from their Chat conversation attached.

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Scope; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationales: risk, impact
claims.claim: Suggestions are shown only for experiences the user can already access, so the card grants no new access.
claims.quote: Users will see suggestions only for experiences they can access. For example, users who do not have access to Cowork will not see a suggestion to use Cowork.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The notice does not specify the mode-selection algorithm or how much conversation context is attached.
claims.quote: if Copilot determines that another Copilot experience available to the user may better fit a request or task, the user may see a banner suggesting that experience.

claims.claim: Microsoft's usage-based billing page lists Cowork as requiring a Copilot licence.

claims.fix: Keep the attribution to the billing page, but add: 'Microsoft's Copilot overview specifies a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence for usage-based billing capabilities, including Cowork.' claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed because Cowork combines a Copilot licence prerequisite with usage-based billing.
claims.quote: This model complements fixed subscription licensing with a flexible payment option that aligns to actual usage. Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.claim: Cowork operates within the user's existing permissions and security boundaries.
claims.quote: It connects to your Outlook, Calendar, Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, and other Microsoft 365 services, operating within your existing permissions and security boundaries.

claims.claim: Cowork carries out multi-step tasks on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot Cowork is an AI-powered agentic system that carries out multi-step tasks on your behalf across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Cowork can send emails.
claims.quote: sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: Cowork can schedule meetings.
claims.quote: sending emails, scheduling meetings, creating documents, posting in Teams, conducting research, and managing files.

claims.claim: Cowork requires explicit user approval for sensitive actions.
claims.quote: Each action is visible in the conversation, and sensitive actions require your explicit approval before they're executed.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is selected by default for spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.claim: Auto-apply new services automatically adds newly supported services unless it is turned off.
claims.quote: When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: The route to a group-scoped Cowork policy is Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Select agents and services > Cowork.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.
claims.fix: Replace the path in controls[1].ui and its rendered row with 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Scope user and group > Specific groups > group > Select agents and services > Cowork'. The existing management source documents the required Identity policy-type choice; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/cowork/cowork-admin-governance documents Scope user and group, Specific groups and Cowork. Selecting the target group is an allowed omission, but choosing Identity rather than a resource-based policy is not.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/serviceSettings/{serviceId} changes a policy's service access setting.

claims.quote: The state property can be updated. Setting state to disabled is the removal semantic

claims.claim: A policy scoped to specific groups grants access to the users in those groups when it selects Cowork.
claims.quote: On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group. On the Select agents and services step, select Cowork.

claims.claim: Precedence among overlapping Cowork policies decides which limits apply rather than whether access is granted.
claims.quote: When a user is in multiple policies that select Cowork, the precedence rules only choose which limits apply—they don't decide whether access is granted.

claims.claim: A more restrictive policy does not override a more permissive Cowork access grant.
claims.quote: Access is decided per service by whether any applicable policy selects that service. A more restrictive policy doesn't override a more permissive one.

claims.claim: The cited Microsoft Graph cost-management operations are beta APIs subject to change.
